title: Economics explained
description: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measures how much India's factories, mines, and power plants are producing. It's like a monthly report card for the c.

faq.q: What is the current base year for India's IIP?
faq.a: The current base year for India's Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is 2022-23. This was updated from the previous base year of 2011-12 in June 2026.

faq.q: How often is the IIP data released?
faq.a: The "Quick Estimate" of the IIP is released monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), usually on the 28th of each month (or the next working day) for the month two months prior.

faq.q: Which sectors contribute most to the IIP?
faq.a: The manufacturing sector has the largest weight in the IIP, followed by mining and electricity.

faq.q: Does the IIP include agricultural production?
faq.a: No, the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) specifically measures the output of the industrial sector, which includes manufacturing, mining, and electricity. It does not include agricultural production.

faq.q: Why is changing the base year important?
faq.a: Changing the base year is important because it ensures the IIP accurately reflects the current structure of India's industries, including new products and technologies, and the changing importance (weights) of different sectors in the economy.

fact_check.summary: The article accurately presents information about the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India, including its new base year and recent growth figures, citing authoritative sources.
